title: The Morality of Probability: How Implicit Moral Biases in LLMs May Shape the Future of Human-AI Symbiosis
benchmark_measurement: The benchmark measured implicit moral biases by having LLMs rank and score outcomes for 18 dilemmas. These outcomes were designed around five moral frameworks, one of which, 'Virtue Value', is explicitly linked to Confucian thought. The paper analyzes how cultural influences from training data, including Confucian and Buddhist ideologies for Chinese models, affect these moral preferences.
findings: Chinese models showed a stronger preference for communitarian and virtue-centered values (Care, Virtue) compared to American models. The paper attributes this to the cultural milieu and training data, which likely include Confucian and Buddhist ideological influences emphasizing benevolence, relational duty, and harmony over individual rights.
